MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Requisition ID: REQ677142
Employment Type: Permanent Part - Time
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Specialist - Grade 2
Remuneration: $128,301.89 - $132,523.13 per annum, pro rata (+ super + 17.5% leave loading where applicable) 
Hours per week:16 
Applications Close: 4 August 2026 
Vaccination Category: A
Located in: Wagga Wagga

Lead When It Matters Most. Be the Calm in Every Emergency

About the Opportunity-
Join the Wagga Wagga Base Hospital After Hours team as a Clinical Nurse Specialist Grade 2 - After Hours Clinical Support and play a vital role in supporting staff and responding to clinical emergencies across the hospital.
Working after hours, you'll provide advanced clinical support, leadership and expert decision-making to nursing and multidisciplinary teams, ensuring safe, timely and high-quality care when senior clinical support is needed most. You'll respond to deteriorating patients, cardiac arrests and medical emergencies, assisting Team Leaders with advanced life support, defibrillation, emergency medication administration and airway, breathing and circulation management.
This autonomous and highly respected role requires advanced clinical judgement, excellent communication skills and the confidence to lead and support staff in complex situations. You'll also mentor nurses, promote evidence-based practice and contribute to a culture of continuous learning, safety and clinical excellence.

About You
Our ideal candidate will have:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA.

Clinical Nurse Specialist Grade 2 qualifications with relevant postgraduate qualifications and at least three years' experience in an acute specialty. 

Current Advanced Life Support (ALS2) certification with demonstrated competence in emergency response, including defibrillation, emergency medications and advanced assessment of airway, breathing and circulation. 

Demonstrated experience managing deteriorating patients and supporting Team Leaders during medical emergencies and cardiac arrests. 

Advanced clinical assessment, critical thinking and decision-making skills with the ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced acute hospital environment. 

Proven leadership, mentoring and communication skills with the ability to support and educate nursing staff while working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams. 

Commitment to evidence-based practice, patient safety, quality improvement and ongoing professional development.

As the Clinical Nurse Consultant, you will:

Demonstrate advanced clinical assessment, decision-making and consultation skills. 

Have the ability to support clinicians through virtual care platforms and complex patient flow processes. 

Be confident coordinating interfacility transfers and navigating competing clinical priorities.

Demonstrate strong leadership, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. 

Be committed to evidence-based practice, quality improvement and service development. 

Thrive in a collaborative multidisciplinary environment and contribute to education, mentoring and capability building across the District.
 

To find out more, please review the Position Description

About You
Our ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Current registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse.

Have minimum 3 years post-registration nursing experience, including at least 3 years recent experience within a critical care environment.

Completion of a Graduate Nurse Program or equivalent

Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.

A strong commitment to person-centred care, cultural safety, and ongoing professional development.

Why join MLHD?

At Murrumbidgee Local Health District (MLHD), we offer more than a job - we offer the chance to make a real difference.

Meaningful Impact - Play a vital role in supporting essential services to our diverse and vibrant regional communities.

Flexible Working Arrangements - Designed to support work-life balance, aligned with NSW Health policy. 

Generous Salary Packaging - Access up to $20,600 per annum tax-free for living expenses, plus the option for novated car leasing.

Professional Development - Take advantage of ongoing learning and career development opportunities.

Health & Wellbeing Support - Benefit from our comprehensive wellness programs for you and your family, including Employee Assistance Programs Fitness Passport and initiatives to support both physical and mental health.

Click here to discover why MLHD is the right place to grow your career and contribute to healthier communities.

How to Apply
If this sounds like the opportunity for you, click apply now! Please contact Verina Walsh, via Verina.Walsh@health.nsw.gov.au if you have any questions about this role.
Your application will need to include:

A current CV

A cover letter

Responses to the application questions

MLHD welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and is committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. 
We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disability, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and the LGBTIQ+ community. 
If you identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, you can access recruitment application support through the Stepping Up initiative.

This is a NSW Health Category A position which requires immunisation and screening for certain diseases. The full list of requirements are outlined in the NSW Health OASV Policy (Page 11). You will be required to complete the OASV Undertaking- Declaration Form and 

TB Assessment Tool during the recruitment process. Please upload this with your application along with any other vaccination evidence that you may have.

Position: Pastrycook
Type: Full-time
Employer: San Antonio Group Pty Ltd
Location: Kirribilli NSW 2061
Salary: $79,423 - $89,423 p/a
About the Business
San Antonio Group Pty Ltd is a well-established bakery specialising in the production of traditional baked goods and confectionery products. The company prepares a wide range of fresh breads, pastries, cakes, desserts, and specialty items daily using both traditional and modern techniques. Products are supplied directly to customers through its retail outlet in Kirribilli, with a strong emphasis on ingredient sourcing, quality control, food safety compliance, and customer satisfaction. Renowned for its commitment to consistency, innovation in recipes, and high presentation standards, the business values integrity, teamwork, and excellence in every batch. The workplace culture fosters a supportive, hygienic, and collaborative environment where staff take pride in delivering exceptional baked goods to the local community.
About the Position
The Pastrycook plays a vital role in San Antonio Group Pty Ltd’s daily operations, responsible for preparing and producing a diverse range of high-quality pastries, cakes, and baked goods according to established recipes and standards. This position involves hands-on production from ingredient preparation through to finishing and packaging, ensuring all items meet the bakery’s strict quality, freshness, and presentation requirements. The role is essential to maintaining the business’s reputation for excellence and supporting timely supply to retail customers in a fast-paced bakery environment.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare and produce a wide range of pastries, cakes and other baked goods in accordance with San Antonio Group's established recipes, production methods and quality standards.
Measure, weigh and prepare ingredients, ensuring all raw materials meet required quality and freshness standards.
Mix, laminate, shape and proof doughs and pastry products using both manual techniques and commercial bakery equipment.
Prepare a variety of pastry fillings, creams, icings and decorative finishes for baked products.
Monitor proofing, baking processes and oven temperatures to ensure products are baked consistently and meet quality and presentation standards.
Coordinate the production process, including preparing, baking, cooling, finishing and packaging bakery products to meet daily production schedules.
Decorate cakes, pastries and desserts using glazes, creams, icings and other finishing techniques to achieve high presentation standards.
Operate and maintain commercial bakery equipment, including mixers, dough sheeters, moulders and ovens, ensuring safe and efficient operation.
Maintain a clean, hygienic and organised work area by cleaning equipment, utensils, baking trays and production areas in accordance with food safety and workplace health and safety requirements.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Baking or a related field.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience as a Pastrycook or in a similar role.
Strong technical skills in pastry production, dough handling, laminating, baking techniques, and cake decoration.
Sound knowledge of food safety and hygiene regulations, with the ability to maintain a clean and safe working environment.
Excellent attention to detail, time management skills, and the ability to work efficiently under pressure to meet production schedules.
Good interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively as part of a small team.
Physical fitness and stamina to stand for extended periods and handle manual tasks.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Role title: Clinical Support Officer

Role type: Maximum Term Part-Time (24hrs-week) until December 2026

Role grade: Administrative Officer Level 2, (Year 1-2)

Department and location: Rehabilitation Unit, St Vincent's Hospital, Darlinghurst

Salary: +$66,608- $68,817 (pro-rata) + super + salary package

Better and fairer care. Always.

We are St Vincent's Health Australia, Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services. 

Founded by The Sisters of Charity in 1857, our +30,000 healthcare superheroes operate public and private hospitals, residential aged care, community and virtual care, and outreach programs. 

About the role

Managing roster and HR data entry, including maintaining electronic rosters, processing approved staffing changes and ensuring workforce records are accurate and up to date.

Supporting workforce administration activities such as recruitment, leave management, payroll enquiries, performance review processes and staff replacement coordination.

Assisting with data management and reporting, including preparing workforce, finance and quality reports and providing administrative support for patient care-related activities.

Coordinating ward-unit resources by monitoring stock levels, arranging the purchase and maintenance of equipment, and ensuring supplies are available to support patient care delivery.

Providing comprehensive administrative support to the multidisciplinary healthcare team, including meeting coordination, scheduling activities, organising travel and accommodation, and supporting ward rounds and other operational functions.

About you

Demonstrated experience in administration within a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage workforce records, rostering and HR data accurately.

Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities and meet deadlines with a high level of attention to detail.

Experience providing administrative support across workforce functions, including recruitment, leave administration, payroll enquiries and staff coordination.

Well-developed computer skills, with experience using Microsoft Office and electronic HR, rostering or patient administration systems to prepare reports and maintain accurate records.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams while maintaining confidentiality and delivering high-quality customer service.

Why work at St Vincent's?

Join us on our mission to provide care to all, including the most at-risk people in our community

Discounted access to many gyms for you and your family with Fitness Passport

Access to discounted private health insurance with Medibank

Access to a government salary sacrifice program. Make a proportion of your salary tax-free

Committed to financial support for educational development, scholarship programs, paid study leave

About the hospital

In this role you will be based at St Vincent's hospital, Darlinghurst. 

A busy inner-city hospital in a beautiful location

Surrounded by great cafes, galleries and theatres, parks, nightlife, and nearby glorious beaches

A place of expert clinical care for at-risk people

Closely partnered with universities & affiliated research institutes, many of which are located on-campus

Centres of excellence include heart & lung transplantation, bone marrow transplantation, cardiology, cancer care, AIDS-HIV, respiratory medicine, mental health, homeless health, drug & alcohol services, and correctional health

Job Title:  Behaviour Support Practitioner - Graduates/Training - Sydney NSW 

  Working hours:  16 - 38 hours / Week (Flexible for part time) 

  Salary : Competitive salary (based on experience) + CPD + Benefits 

  Location:  Sydney, NSW 

  About the role  
Our client is seeking passionate and driven experienced Proficient Behaviour Support Practitioners to work with a diverse caseload of Mental Health, Physical, ASD, Cognitive/Neuro – 75% adults. Ideally, you will have knowledge and confidence with the following: 

 
	 Demonstrate ability to conduct comprehensive behaviour assessments and designing, implementing and evaluating behaviour support plans 
	 Understanding of  evidence-based  principles and relevant standards 
	 Demonstrate an awareness of the principles of positive behavioural intervention, including strategies that are embedded in the context of strengths based and least restrictive practices 
	 Support NDIS participants’ inclusion and participation in the community 
	 Demonstrate a range of intervention strategies to address needs that relate to activities of daily living, social integration, sensory processing and integration and mental health management 
	 Participate in regular professional development opportunities to keep up with current developments 
 

  Requirements:  

 
	 Current professional body registration (where appropriate) 
	 Experience as a behavioral support practitioner (preferred) 
	 NDIS Worker Screening Clearance 
	 Working with Children’s check 
	 Current Driver’s license 
	 Ability to effectively communicate with parents and carers. 
	 A passion for helping people with behavioural difficulties
